title: ACME Edge Pilot: Scope, Kickoff Agenda, and Acceptance Criteria
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc frames the kickoff and acceptance criteria for ACME Retail’s ‘Edge Personalization’ pilot. ACME wants an on-prem/edge inference topology to run small but latency-sensitive personalization queries in their retail kiosks. Solutions Eng will validate functional fit, performance (latency/throughput), cost model, and operational runbook for a minimal production path.

High-level objectives (what success looks like for the Pilot):
- Functional: Personalized product recommendations generated from customer session data with slot-filling responses that include product id + short rationale.
- Performance: Median (P50) inference latency <= 80ms for 32-token responses; P95 <= 220ms during baseline load.
- Throughput: Each kiosk should support sustained 8 qps with occasional bursts to 20 qps without failing SLOs.
- Cost/op economics: Projected per-kiosk inference cost < $0.10 per 1k inference calls at steady-state configuration (estimates using quantized 8-bit model and batching).
- Quality: Top-1 recommendation relevance >= 68% on the validation prompt set (human-labeled), with hallucination incidents <= 2% as measured by the evaluation sampling procedure.
- Operability: Automated health checks + cold-start recovery documented; alerting thresholds validated in the pilot.

Scope (in-scope for this POC):
- Deployment topology: Private (on-prem) single-GPU inference host per kiosk region (edge aggregator), with a lightweight local cache for recent session prefix KV.
- Models: Evaluate two model variants: base open-weights 7B quantized and a distilled 3B variant.
- Data: Use synthetic sessions + sanitized historical logs provided by ACME (PII stripped) and a small set (n=300) of hand-labeled prompts for quality eval.
- Integrations: HTTP API compatibility with ACME kiosk software (JSON request/response), and metrics export to Prometheus pushgateway.
- Timeline: 6 weeks from kickoff to acceptance review.

Out-of-scope for this Pilot:
- Full multi-region private control plane deployment (we’ll simulate region failover via manual steps).
- Custom model training or fine-tuning beyond light prompt engineering and instruction tuning via few-shot examples.

Quantitative acceptance criteria (must pass all to be marked accepted):
1) Latency SLOs: P50 <= 80ms and P95 <= 220ms on the evaluation harness running production-like traffic patterns for 30 minutes.
2) Availability: 99.5% successful requests over a 24-hour soak test (allowing maintenance restarts).
3) Relevance: Top-1 recommendation relevance >= 68% on the curated human-labeled set (n=300).
4) Hallucination rate: <= 2% on a 200-sample random audit. Hallucination defined as responses that assert false facts about inventory or pricing.
5) Resource utilization: GPU memory headroom >= 10% at steady state for chosen config (to allow caching/bursting).
6) Observability: Logs, traces, per-request token cost, and a dashboard with P50/P95 latencies must be in place and exercised during acceptance run.
7) Security: Encryption at rest for model artifacts and TLS for in-cluster RPCs validated; an audit checklist must be signed by ACME security contact.

Acceptance test plan (how we measure):
- Test harness: Solutions Eng will run a synthetic driver that replays 100k sessions over 24 hours with varying session lengths to exercise batching and caching.
- Live validation: Run 500 live kiosk requests during business hours with ACME product specialists confirming perceived relevance.
- Manual audit: Random sample of 200 responses reviewed by ACME subject matter experts for hallucination and compliance.
- Cost modeling: Run throughput curves to estimate token/sec and amortized cost; produce per-kiosk monthly cost projection.

Kickoff workshop agenda (90-minute remote workshop):
- 0–10m: Introductions, objectives recap (Samira)
- 10–25m: ACME product/context walkthrough (ACME PM: Laura Chen)
- 25–40m: Proposed topology and model variants (Ethan Morales)
- 40–55m: Data requirements, sanitization, and sample exchange plan (Priya Nair + ACME data lead)
- 55–70m: Acceptance criteria deep-dive and metrics instrumentation (Jules Park)
- 70–80m: Risk register: security, bandwidth, and on-device constraints (Noah Bennett)
- 80–90m: Immediate next steps and owners; schedule 1-week technical syncs

Roles & responsibilities:
- Solutions Eng (Samira lead): overall account technical lead, acceptance tests, deployment scripts, and on-call during soak.
- Platform Eng (Ethan): build and tune the inference container image and quantization profile.
- Data & Privacy (Priya): validate data sanitization, run labeling instructions, and coordinate sample exchange.
- ACME (Laura Chen, ACME Security): provide sanitized logs, sign security checklist, and lead manual audits.

Operational runbook highlights (to be expanded in repo):
- Startup sequence: container start -> model load -> KV cache warmup -> readiness probe passes. Estimated load/generation warmup: 60–120s.
- Health checks: p95 latency > 350ms sustained for 2m triggers alert; GPU mem usage > 92% for 3m triggers scaling/fallover.
- Failure modes & rollback: if P95 > 400ms for 10m, automatically switch traffic to distilled 3B variant.
- Logging: per-request token counts, prompt/response hashes (no raw user text stored), error counters.

Data security & compliance notes:
- ACME will provide logs with PII redaction performed in their environment. Solutions Eng will only receive sanitized samples and hashed identifiers.
- Model artifacts will be stored encrypted (AES-256) on local volumes; keys referenced via customer KMS (ACME-managed).
- Network: restrict egress; allow only pre-approved endpoints for metrics and artifact fetch.

Technical approach summary:
- Serve runtime: Redwood’s on-prem inference container with continuous batching enabled.
- Kernel selection: test two configs — default optimized kernels for 7B quantized and a lightweight kernel path for distilled 3B.
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache for session-level context; configure 1k-entry LRU with 24h TTL for session tokens.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Network bandwidth at kiosk aggregator is lower than expected -> Mitigation: measure baseline bandwidth during pilot setup; reduce model size to 3B variant and increase local caching.
- Risk: Relevance below threshold -> Mitigation: run prompt engineering sessions, adjust temperature/hyperparams and consider light dataset instruction tuning if necessary (out-of-scope for the pilot but flagged for follow-up).
- Risk: Security sign-off delayed -> Mitigation: prioritize the security checklist and run a minimal test with sanitized synthetic data until sign-off.

Deliverables by end of pilot:
- Deployment artifacts: helm-lite chart + container image tag, quantization profiles, and tunable config file.
- Runbook: condensed operational playbook and incident run-steps.
- Evaluation report: latency/throughput graphs, relevance/hallucination audit, and cost projection.
- Acceptance sign-off: one-page checklist signed by Solutions Eng and ACME product/security leads.

Immediate next steps (owners and dates):
- [Samira] Draft deployment checklist and repo skeleton by 2025-02-21.
- [ACME / Laura] Provide sanitized sample logs (n=5k sessions) by 2025-02-24.
- [Ethan] Build initial container with 7B quantized profile and push image tag by 2025-02-28.
- [Priya] Prepare labeling instructions and start batch labeling for 300 validation prompts by 2025-03-01.
- Schedule: First technical sync 2025-02-25, 30 min standing twice/week.

Notes / open questions for kickoff: 
- Does ACME require on-device inference (per-kiosk) or a regional aggregator per 50 kiosks? (ACME to confirm.)
- Can ACME share realistic bandwidth logs during shopping hours to better simulate network constraints?
- Security: confirm KMS onboarding window and how keys will be rotated.

Appendix: evaluation rubric examples (short)
- Relevance score: 0/1 per sample where 1 = recommendation meets business rule and matches at least one relevant product in ground truth.
- Hallucination flag: binary per-sample plus short notes.
- Latency buckets: P50, P90, P95, error-rate at each bucket.

If accepted, we will produce a concise acceptance certificate and transition items for Dedicated/Private long-term deployment planning.

Document owner for clarifications: Samira Khan (samira.khan@redwood.ai)
